question: Which body part houses the organs for the special senses?
explanation: Special sense organs like the eyes, ears, and nose are all localized in the head region. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T1#GNS311_U3_T1_h1)

question: What is sensory transduction?

options.A: Converting environmental stimuli into electrical signals

explanation: Transduction is the translation of physical or chemical stimuli into electrical nerve impulses that the brain can understand. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T1#GNS311_U3_T1_h1)

question: Which retinal photoreceptor cell is responsible for color vision?
explanation: Cone cells operate best in bright light and allow the perception of fine details and distinct colors. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T1#GNS311_U3_T1_h2)

question: A patient struggles to see in dim hospital corridors at night. Which retinal cells are likely underperforming?
explanation: Rods are specialized photoreceptors that function primarily in low-light environments for night and peripheral vision. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T1#GNS311_U3_T1_h2)

question: Name the three auditory ossicles found in the middle ear.
explanation: The middle ear contains three small interconnected bones—the malleus, incus, and stapes—that transmit sound vibrations. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T1#GNS311_U3_T1_h3)

question: Damage to the semicircular canals of the inner ear will most likely cause what symptom?
explanation: The semicircular canals are part of the vestibular system responsible for detecting head movement and maintaining balance. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T1#GNS311_U3_T1_h3)

question: Where are the primary olfactory receptors located?

options.B: On the cornea of the eye

explanation: Olfactory receptors reside in the superior portion of the nasal cavity where they detect airborne chemical odorants. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T1#GNS311_U3_T1_h4)

question: Why does severe nasal congestion make food taste bland?

options.B: Cranial nerves are crushed by swelling
options.C: Olfactory input is blocked, reducing flavor perception
options.D: Taste buds are paralyzed by viruses

explanation: Much of what we perceive as taste relies on the sense of smell working in tandem with gustatory receptors. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T1#GNS311_U3_T1_h4)

question: Which major brain structure acts as the relay station for almost all sensory pathways?
explanation: The thalamus processes and relays sensory signals to the appropriate regions of the cerebral cortex, with the sole exception of smell. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T1#GNS311_U3_T1_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of sensory adaptation?

options.D: Preventing sensory overload from constant stimuli

explanation: Sensory adaptation allows nerve receptors to slow down their firing when exposed to continuous, non-threatening stimuli. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T1#GNS311_U3_T1_h5)

question: What term describes the natural age-related hearing loss affecting high-frequency sounds?
explanation: Presbycusis is the gradual, sensorineural hearing loss associated with aging, typically impacting higher frequencies first. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T1#GNS311_U3_T1_h6)

question: An elderly patient has decreased touch and temperature sensation. What is an important safety intervention?

options.A: Apply scented lotions every two hours
options.C: Check bathwater temperature with a thermometer

explanation: Patients with impaired touch and temperature senses are at high risk for accidental scald injuries, requiring nurse-verified water temperatures. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T1#GNS311_U3_T1_h6)
